clue.text: Invocation to Beelzebub

parts.note: surface reading: a prayer or summoning call addressed to the prince of demons
setter's reading: the saying uttered when someone you were just discussing walks in, as if naming Satan summoned him

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads like occult ritual; the answer is the everyday idiom said when the person under discussion turns up, which treats mention as summoning.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb holds that mentioning Satan makes him appear, so uttering the phrase is playfully a summons of the fiend.

clue.text: In Celtic practices Idris gets mud-spattered

indicators.note: something spattered is splashed about and scattered, so the letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Welshman called Idris ends up splashed with mud while joining in some ancient Celtic rites.
explanation.walkthrough: Idris is a Welsh name, fitting the Celtic surface; 'mud-spattered' hides both the second piece of fodder and the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Druidism is the religion and ritual of the ancient Celtic priesthood, so it names those Celtic observances.

clue.text: To keep changing channels should come up with a gem

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up means reading the word from bottom to top

parts.note: to zap is to flick rapidly between TV channels with the remote

explanation.surface: A channel-hopping viewer is told their restless remote use will turn up a jewel.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the second piece turns upwards; the first stays as it is in front of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Topaz is a precious stone, typically yellow or amber, so it is an example of a gem.

clue.text: One whose hands are gainfully occupied

definitions.text: One whose hands are gainfully occupied

parts.words: One whose hands are gainfully occupied
parts.note: surface reading: a busy person whose own hands are kept at profitable work
setter's reading: hands are workers or staff, and this person keeps them in paid jobs

explanation.walkthrough: 'Hands' reads as body parts, but it means farmhands or factory hands: hired workers, whom this person gives paid work.
explanation.definitionFit: A boss who hires staff keeps those workers in paid work, so the hired hands are gainfully occupied by them.

clue.text: Minister can be a nuisance about the teaching of scripture

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece wraps round the other

parts.note: a pest is an annoying person or thing
RI is religious instruction, the old school subject

explanation.surface: A clergyman can be tiresome when he goes on about Bible lessons.
explanation.walkthrough: RI, religious instruction, was the name for scripture lessons in British schools.
explanation.definitionFit: A minister of religion is a clergyman, and in many churches such an ordained cleric is called by this title.

clue.text: A good deal signified, they say, by a piece of ground

indicators.note: what they say is heard spoken, so the sound counts rather than the spelling

parts.note: a good deal is a lot, and signified is meant

explanation.surface: Someone claims a plot of land carries great significance.
explanation.walkthrough: An allotment is a small plot of land rented from a British council for growing vegetables.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a share of land assigned to a person, typically a garden plot for cultivation.

clue.text: Rigorous way to limit endless fiddle

indicators.note: to limit something is to bound it on both sides, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a way

indicators.note: without an end, the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a fiddle is a swindle or trick

explanation.surface: A strict method is proposed for curbing a never-ending swindle.
explanation.walkthrough: The street abbreviation opens up so that the shortened trick sits between its S and T.
explanation.definitionFit: Strict and rigorous are synonyms: both describe something exacting, demanding precise adherence to rules.

clue.text: Commercial enticement for the acquisitive

parts.note: surface reading: some lure or bait used by sellers to tempt greedy shoppers
setter's reading: a commercial is a TV advert, and the answer is the stock phrase its voiceover uses to promise extras

explanation.walkthrough: 'Commercial' seems an adjective but points to the TV advert, whose announcer piles on extras with this breathless catchphrase.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a cliché of advertising, promising buyers yet more goods on top of what was listed.

clue.text: Entertainer going through the newspaper for meronyms

indicators.note: the answer goes through several words, running across their boundaries

parts.note: the end of the first word, the whole second word and the start of the third

explanation.surface: An entertainer searches the paper for meronyms, words naming a part of a whole.
explanation.walkthrough: The odd word meronyms is there only to supply the closing letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A performer is anyone who entertains an audience, such as an actor, singer or musician.

clue.text: The language of the City — money

parts.note: LA is Los Angeles, a city
tin is old slang for money

explanation.surface: The financial City of London is said to speak only the tongue of cash.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital C suggests the City of London, its financial district; here it is just a city, Los Angeles.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin was the tongue of ancient Rome and long the language of learning and the Church.

clue.text: Girl calls for a large beer

indicators.note: a call is something spoken, so the sound of the request matters

parts.note: a large beer is a big ale

explanation.surface: A young woman at the bar orders a big pint.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken quickly, the order for a big glass of ale runs together into a name.
explanation.definitionFit: Abigail is a female first name, and once also a word for a lady's maid, so it suits a girl.

clue.text: "Moi" gets construed as conceit

indicators.note: to construe is to interpret or rearrange the sense, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Saying 'Moi?' in the Miss Piggy manner is taken as a sign of vanity.
explanation.definitionFit: Egotism is excessive self-regard, which is what conceit means: an inflated opinion of oneself.

clue.text: Duck noise, by god!

parts.note: a duck is a score of nought in cricket, shaped like the letter O
a din is a loud noise

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims at the racket a duck is making.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By god!' reads as an oath; it is a link word and the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Odin is the chief deity of Norse mythology, father of Thor, so he is a god.

clue.text: Methodical distribution of city's steam

indicators.note: distributing spreads things out to new places, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, apostrophe dropped
taken as written

explanation.surface: A city's district-heating steam is piped out in an orderly way.
explanation.definitionFit: Systematic and methodical are synonyms: both mean following an orderly plan or procedure.

clue.text: Anticipate everyone's after lots of trees

indicators.note: is after places one piece behind the other in the answer

parts.note: a forest is a large area of trees
everyone is all

explanation.surface: Someone expects everybody to be chasing after timber.
explanation.definitionFit: To forestall is to act in advance to prevent something, the sense of anticipate as getting in first.

clue.text: Early reading-desk found in back furrow with drum

indicators.note: found in means sitting inside another piece
going back means reading the word in the opposite direction

parts.note: a rut is a furrow or groove
an ambo is a raised lectern in early Christian churches

explanation.surface: An old lectern turns up in a ploughed groove alongside a drum.
explanation.walkthrough: An ambo is a pulpit-like reading desk in early churches; it sits inside the turned-round furrow.
explanation.definitionFit: A tambour is a drum, especially a small one or a bass drum; the word is French for drum.

clue.text: Trick hard to verify

parts.note: a con is a trick or swindle
firm means hard or solid

explanation.surface: A tricky deception is difficult to check.
explanation.definitionFit: To confirm something is to establish that it is true, which is what verify means.

clue.text: Paddler on his own may be an independent type?

definitions.text: Paddler on his own may be an independent type?

parts.note: surface reading: a solitary wader at the seaside
setter's reading: to paddle your own boat is the idiom for being self-reliant, so this boater suggests independence

explanation.walkthrough: The idiom 'paddle your own canoe' means to manage on your own; the answer is someone who literally does it.
explanation.definitionFit: This sportsperson propels a light boat with a paddle, literally acting out the saying about self-reliance.

clue.text: Native to this place entering local, the Turk's Head

indicators.note: entering means going inside another piece

parts.note: a local is a neighbourhood pub, here an inn
this place is here

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the opening letter of Turk

explanation.surface: A pub called the Turk's Head is said to belong to the neighbourhood.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain your 'local' is your regular nearby pub; Turk's Head is a common pub name.
explanation.definitionFit: Inherent means existing as a natural, built-in part of something, so it is native to it.

clue.text: Growing red during brute scene in play

indicators.note: something in play is moving and loose, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A theatregoer blushes during a violent scene on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In play' suggests a stage play, fitting the theatre surface, but it is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Erubescent is a rare formal word meaning reddening or blushing, from the Latin for becoming red.

clue.text: Green, straggly juniper must be lopped

indicators.note: straggly growth sprawls untidily, so the letters are disordered
lopping cuts off a top part, so the first letter goes

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An untidy, overgrown juniper bush needs pruning.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue the top of the shrub is lopped, so its first letter goes before the rest is shuffled.
explanation.definitionFit: Green fruit is not yet ripe, so in this sense green is a synonym for immature.

clue.text: Search for volunteers to turn up and fight

parts.note: to comb is to search thoroughly

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means reading upwards, so the word runs backwards

parts.note: the TA, Territorial Army, was Britain's volunteer reserve force

explanation.surface: A recruiter looks for volunteers to turn out and go to war.
explanation.walkthrough: The Territorial Army, TA, was Britain's part-time volunteer army reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: Combat is fighting, especially armed conflict between forces, so the noun matches fight.

clue.text: Companion I begin to cherish has style

parts.note: CH is Companion of Honour, a British order
taken as written

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter only

parts.note: the opening letter of cherish

explanation.surface: A friend begins to treasure someone who is elegant.
explanation.walkthrough: CH stands for Companion of Honour, a British honour; read 'has' as joining wordplay to the noun definition.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun chic means stylishness or elegance, so it can stand for style itself.

clue.text: Chance to split

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an opportunity, as in a lucky opening
second meaning: to divide or snap into pieces

explanation.definitionFit: The word is a noun meaning a lucky opportunity and a verb meaning to come apart or shatter.

clue.text: Speechless about a bishop taken aback by misprint

indicators.note: taken aback suggests being pushed backwards, so the whole is read in reverse
about means going around, so one piece wraps another

parts.note: mute means unable to speak
taken as written
RR is Right Reverend, the title of a bishop

explanation.surface: A bishop is left dumbstruck by a printing error.
explanation.walkthrough: A bishop is styled the Right Reverend, abbreviated RR.
explanation.definitionFit: Erratum is the Latin-derived term for an error in printing or writing, listed on a correction slip.

clue.text: Sound transmitter with whiskers doesn't start? That's odd!

indicators.note: not starting means the first letter is missing

parts.note: whiskers on the face form a beard
rum is British slang for odd or strange

explanation.surface: Someone is puzzled that a bearded device will not switch on.
explanation.walkthrough: Rum is old British slang for strange; the beard loses its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The tympanic membrane vibrates with incoming sound waves and passes them on to the inner ear's bones.

clue.text: Bit of a wimp, Elmer; you've got to push forward

indicators.note: a bit of the text is a part of it, lying across the words

parts.note: runs across the two names, ignoring the comma

explanation.surface: Elmer is told he is something of a weakling and must press on.
explanation.definitionFit: To impel is to drive or urge forward, so it is a synonym for push forward.

clue.text: Dry sort of person to place marker at the back of a book

indicators.note: at the back means placed after, so one piece follows the other

parts.note: taken as written
B is the abbreviation for book
a stainer is one who marks or stains

explanation.surface: A dull reader is told to put a bookmark at the end of a volume.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dry' looks like boring, but means teetotal; 'marker' is literal: something that leaves stains.
explanation.definitionFit: A dry person drinks no alcohol, and a teetotaller is exactly one who refrains from drink.
